notes: Read all 127 source lines line by line before editing. The web file is React Router v6's <ScrollRestoration> re-implemented for the classic <BrowserRouter>: per-location-key scroll save/restore, POP restores, PUSH/REPLACE scroll-to-top, operating on the <main id=main-content> DOM scroll container with a window fallback. All behavior, the STORAGE_PREFIX, and helper semantics are preserved.

L1 react hooks -> imported useCallback/useEffect/useLayoutEffect/useMemo/useRef. L2 react-router useLocation/useNavigationType have no native analogue, so location/navigation arrive as native-safe props (pathname/search/navType: ScrollNavigationType) supplied by the native navigation shell, matching the RouteAnnouncer parity convention.

L4-29 doc comment -> ported and adapted to document the native-safe replacements. L31 STORAGE_PREFIX 'teslasync.scroll:' preserved verbatim. L33-35 keyFor preserved verbatim (`${STORAGE_PREFIX}${pathname}${search}`).

L37-46 readSaved and L48-55 writeSaved -> ported 1:1 against a module-level in-memory Map (scrollSessionStore) that replaces the unavailable browser sessionStorage. Values are kept as strings so the getItem/Number()/Number.isFinite read parsing and setItem(String(value)) write semantics are identical; the try/catch no-op-on-failure contract is preserved. The Map's lifetime (survives in-session navigation, not an app restart) mirrors sessionStorage surviving a navigation but not a tab close; resetScrollSessionStore() exposes the implicit tab-close reset.

L57-60 getScrollEl (document.getElementById('main-content')) -> replaced by a ScrollView scrollRef prop (no DOM/getElementById on native). L62-66 getScrollTop (live target.scrollTop / window.scrollY read) -> replaced by a latestOffset ref tracked from the ScrollView onScroll event, since RN has no synchronous offset read. L68-75 setScrollTop (target.scrollTop= / window.scrollTo) -> ScrollView.scrollTo({y, animated:false}); the missing-container case is a no-op, parity with the web window fallback that has no native analogue.

L77-127 ScrollRestoration component -> split into the working useNativeScrollRestoration hook plus a parity ScrollRestoration component that returns null (matching the web return null) and is mounted once near the navigation root. L80 lastKey ref preserved; L82-100 save-on-scroll effect -> the rAF-throttled writer is moved into the onScroll handler (the web global addEventListener('scroll') has no native global source) with a scheduled ref preserving the once-per-frame throttle and reading event.nativeEvent.contentOffset.y. L96 requestAnimationFrame -> scheduleFrame helper that uses globalThis.requestAnimationFrame when present and falls back to setTimeout under Jest (mirrors the established useLogStream native-safe pattern). L103-107 cleanup final-flush preserved in the effect cleanup; removeEventListener (L106) has no native analogue (handler lifetime is owned by the ScrollView).

L110-124 restore effect -> preserved as useLayoutEffect for pre-paint timing; L117-123 POP restores readSaved(key) ?? 0 else scroll-to-top 0, with latestOffset synced to the imperative scroll so it matches the web live-DOM read. L126 return null preserved. SCROLL_EVENT_THROTTLE_MS (16) is surfaced for the owning ScrollView's scrollEventThrottle to reproduce the per-frame write cadence.

No DOM-only modules, browser HTML elements, Recharts, Leaflet, react-router, or old web UI components are imported — only React hooks and React Native ScrollView/NativeScrollEvent/NativeSyntheticEvent types. nativeScrollRestorationCapabilities records the unavailable browser capabilities (react-router location/nav type, sessionStorage, DOM scroll container, window scroll) and the in-memory store + rAF availability for explicit, inspectable unavailable state per rule 7.
Gates run from apps/native: npm run typecheck (tsc --noEmit), npm run lint -- --quiet (eslint), npm test -- --runInBand --detectOpenHandles (jest) — all green.
